title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 13-15 of this numbered sequence): X is a compact oriented surface carrying a combinatorial triangular map, with all faces triangles. A 'pondération' (weighting) of the map is a labelling of the corners of each triangle by the three 'weights', equivalently by 0, 1 and ∞. Equivalently, it is a 3-colouring of the vertices such that every triangle sees all three colours. Such a labelling is the same as a cellular map X → P^1 ramified only over {0,1,∞}, taking each face onto one of the two triangles of the standard 'two-triangle' sphere. In other words, it is a Belyi-type structure for which the triangulation is the pull-back of the real line.

Construction. Over the set of faces there is a natural S_3-torsor: for each face, the set of bijections from its vertices to {0,1,∞}. It is glued across each edge, because the shared edge determines how labels propagate. This gives a ramified S_3-covering X' → X, the 'naturally weighted' covering of the previous page.
- Away from the faces, the covering can ramify only at vertices.
- At a vertex it is unramified iff the vertex order is even.
- The necessary conditions for weightability are: all faces triangles, no folded edges or monogons, all vertex orders even. When they hold, X' → X is an unramified S_3-torsor, and pondérations correspond 1-1 to its global sections.

Refinement in the oriented case. Push the torsor along the sign map sg: S_3 → {±1}. Sections of the resulting double cover X'/S_3^+ are the 'colourings' of the faces by + and -, with adjacent faces of different colours (the dual graph is bipartite). Once such a colouring is fixed, which is the content of this page, the structure group reduces to S_3^+ = A_3 ≅ Z/3. One obtains a canonical principal Z/3-covering X'^+ → X.
- Its isomorphism class is cl(X) ∈ H^1(X, Z/3Z), equation (43).
- cl(X) = 0 is necessary and sufficient for a pondération to exist.
- The pondérations in which the + faces are exactly the faces that are positively oriented (for the given orientation, i.e. the cyclic order 0→1→∞) correspond 1-1 to sections of this Z/3-torsor. For connected X there are therefore 0 or 3 such pondérations, the 3 differing by cyclic relabelling of {0,1,∞}.

Purpose. This characterises which triangulated surfaces are canonical triangulations attached to Belyi maps or dessins (the 'pondérable' cartes). It belongs to the combinatorial-to-algebraic dictionary of the Teichmüller / dessins programme. The next page begins the study of combinatorial polygons and their canonical realisation on P^1_C.
errors: No substantive error. Minor gap: 1-1 correspondence and the 0-or-3 count presuppose X connected. The obstruction class depends on the chosen face colouring; the two colourings of a connected surface give classes related by the outer automorphism of Z/3, so vanishing is independent of the choice. 'Pour l'orientation donnée' tacitly fixes which cyclic order of (0,1,∞) counts as positive.

ideas.what: S_3-torsor of vertex labellings of the faces of a triangulation; it is unramified at a vertex iff the vertex degree is even, and weightings (vertex 3-colourings) are its sections.
ideas.modern_name: Monodromy / colouring torsor of an even (Eulerian) triangulation; generalisation of Heawood's theorem
ideas.usually_credited_to: Heawood (1898) for the sphere case; S. Fisk (1970s 'geometric coloring theory'); later Mohar, Archdeacon and others on 3-colourability of even triangulations of surfaces
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses dessins and canonical triangulations but not, as far as I know, this obstruction class

ideas.what: Reduction to A_3 ≅ Z/3 via a bipartite face colouring, giving an obstruction class cl(X) ∈ H^1(X, Z/3) to the existence of a pondération.
ideas.modern_name: Z/3 cohomological obstruction to vertex 3-colourability of an even triangulation of an orientable surface
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Fisk's work and in later work on even triangulations and the monodromy group of triangulations (e.g. Grannell–Griggs–Knor–Širáň)

ideas.what: Pondérable triangular maps = triangulations obtained as pull-backs of the real line under a map to P^1 ramified over 0, 1, ∞.
ideas.modern_name: Clean dessins / canonical triangulation of a Belyi pair

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates the combinatorial question 'is an even triangulation 3-vertex-colourable?' as the vanishing of a torsor class in H^1(X, Z/3), and links it directly to Belyi / dessin structures. This parallels contemporaneous graph-theoretic work (Fisk) that is not usually connected with dessins d'enfants, though the mathematics itself is elementary and essentially known.
missed.quote: cl(X) ∈ H^1(X, Z/3Z) qu'on peut considérer comme l'obstruction à l'existence d'une pondération, pour la carte triangulaire X
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is only a minor bridge between topological graph theory (colourings of even triangulations) and the dessins literature; it is of historical interest rather than a new result.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean but elementary torsor-theoretic obstruction. The result is essentially Heawood/Fisk-type colouring theory recast cohomologically. It is a nice unpublished framing within the dessins programme, but not new mathematics.

The crossed-out fragment after the covering reads something like 'X^+ → X ... cl X', replaced by 'X'^+ → X''; '(*)' is a marginal marker.
Line 'pour lesquelles les faces + sont les faces [+ ... directes?] (pour l'orientation donnée)': a word, probably 'directes' or similar, seems to be lost between 'faces' and '(pour'.
